q: 1. Closed traverse is suitable in the survey of
explain: A closed traverse, which returns to its starting point, is suitable for surveying areas that form a closed loop, like the boundary of a pond/lake; rivers, roads and coastlines are elongated features better surveyed by open traverses.

q: 2. For the locating a distant object visible from two transit stations, the method usually preferred to, is
options: angles and distance from transit stations
angle from one transit station and distance from the other
explain: For a distant, inaccessible object visible from two transit stations, the method of intersection (angles observed from both known stations) is generally preferred since distances to the object are unknown/inaccessible.

q: 3. The most reliable method of plotting a theodolite traverse is
options: by consecutive co-ordinates of each station
by independent co-ordinate of each station
by plotting included angles and scaling off each traverse
by the tangent method of plotting
explain: Plotting by independent (total) co-ordinates of each station, computed from a common origin, is the most reliable method since errors do not accumulate progressively as they would with consecutive co-ordinates.

q: 4. The orthographical projection of a traverse leg upon the reference meridian is known as
explain: The projection of a traverse leg onto the north-south reference meridian (parallel to the meridian) is called its latitude.

q: 5. The co-ordinate of a point measured perpendicular to the parallel is called
explain: The perpendicular distance of a point from a reference meridian, measured parallel to the parallel (east-west), is called the meridian distance (or total departure) of that point.

q: 6. Total latitude of a point is positive if it lies
explain: By convention, latitude is taken as positive (northing) when the point lies north of the reference parallel, and negative (southing) when south.

q: 7. The altitude of a traverse leg is obtained by multiplying its length by
explain: Latitude of a traverse leg = length x cosine of its reduced bearing, since latitude is the projection along the north-south meridian direction.

q: 8. In a closed traverse, sum of south latitudes exceeds the sum of north latitudes and the sum of east departures exceeds the sum of west departures then, the closing line will lie in
explain: If the net latitude is southward and the net departure is eastward, the closing error vector points south-east, so the closing line to balance it lies in the opposite (north-west) quadrant.

q: 9. The operation of making the algebraic sum of latitudes and departures of a closed traverse, each equal to zero, is known
explain: Adjusting all latitudes and departures so their algebraic sums each equal zero (removing closing error) is collectively known as 'balancing the traverse'.

q: 10. If the angular measurements of a traverse are more precise than its linear measurements, balancing of the traverse, is done by
explain: The transit rule is used when angular measurements are more precise than linear measurements, distributing closing error in proportion to the latitude/departure of each leg rather than its length.

q: 11. The distance between terminal points computed from a subsidiary traverse run between them, is generally known as
explain: When a subsidiary (auxiliary) traverse is run between two points to establish the distance between them, the computed distance is called the traverse base.

q: 12. A plumb bob is required
options: when measuring distances along slopes in a hilly country
for accurate centering of a theodolite over a station mark
for testing the verticality of ranging poles
explain: A plumb bob is a versatile tool used for centering instruments, checking verticality of poles, and transferring points down slopes - so all the listed uses are valid.

q: 13. The most reliable method of plotting a theodolite traverse is
options: by consecutive co-ordinates of each station
by independent co-ordinates of each station
by plotting included angles and scaling off each traverse leg
by the tangent method of plotting
explain: Plotting by independent (total) co-ordinates of each station, computed from the origin, avoids the accumulation of plotting errors that occurs when each point is plotted relative to the previous one (consecutive co-ordinates), making it the most reliable method.

q: 14. The latitude of a traverse leg is obtained by multiplying its length by
explain: Latitude (the north-south component) of a traverse leg = Length x cosine(reduced bearing), since latitude is the projection of the line onto the north-south axis.

q: 15. The operation of making the algebraic sum of latitudes and departures of a closed traverse, each equal to zero, is known
explain: Adjusting all the latitudes and departures of a closed traverse so that their algebraic sums each become zero (removing the closing error) is called balancing the traverse.

q: 16. In a closed traverse
options: the difference between fore bearing & back bearing should be 90°
the sum of included angles should be (2N-4) right angle, where N is the number of sides
the sum of inclined angles should be (2N-1), where N is the number of sides
explain: The geometric property of a closed polygon dictates that the sum of the interior angles is given by the formula (2N - 4) x 90 degrees.

q: 17. Right face and left reading are taken to
options: eliminate error of trunnion axis not exactly horizontal
eliminate error in the line of collimation.
explain: Taking observations in both the face-left and face-right positions and averaging them eliminates errors due to non-collimation (line of sight not perpendicular to the trunnion axis) as well as several other instrumental errors.

q: 18. In a closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is
explain: For a closed traverse, the algebraic sum of all the deflection angles (right deflections positive, left negative) is always equal to 360 degrees.

q: 19. Under ordinary conditions, the precision of a theodolite traverse is affected by
explain: Under ordinary field conditions, systematic linear errors (such as those from a mis-calibrated tape) most significantly affect the precision of a theodolite traverse, since they accumulate consistently rather than cancel out.

q: 20. When internal angles are to be subtended by a theodolite survey for closed traverse
options: exterior angles are measured when the traverse goes anti-clockwise.
explain: To measure the internal (interior) angles of a closed traverse correctly and consistently, the traverse should be run in the counter-clockwise direction.

q: 21. When the first object is to be focused, the scale, is set to 0 deg 00'00" and then
options: the upper screw is fixed , lower screw released, the object sighted, lower screw fixed and lower tangent screw operated
both the clamp screw fixed, to tangent screw operated
bottom clamp screw fixed, top screw released, the object sighted and upper tangent screw operated
object is exactly bisected by operating both the upper and lower tangent screws whichever is convenient.
explain: The standard procedure to set an initial zero reading is: fix the upper clamp, release the lower clamp, roughly sight the object, then fix the lower clamp and use the lower tangent screw to bisect the object exactly.

q: 22. In precision theodolite traverse for roads and railways, the angular error of closure should not exceed
explain: For precision theodolite traverses used in road/railway alignment, the permissible angular error of closure is taken as 30 seconds multiplied by the square root of the number of stations (N).

q: 23. The projection of a traverse line on a line perpendicular to the meridian is known as
explain: As per the book's printed answer key, this projection (onto a line perpendicular to the meridian) is designated as the latitude of the line in this text, though standard convention typically calls this the departure - readers should verify against their copy.

q: 24. The projection of a traverse line on a line parallel to the meridian is known as ... of the line
explain: As per the book's printed answer key, this projection (onto a line parallel to the meridian) is designated departure in this text, though standard convention typically calls this the latitude - readers should verify against their copy.

q: 25. The process of turning the telescope about the vertical axis in horizontal plane is known as
explain: Rotating the telescope about the vertical axis in a horizontal plane (left or right) is called swinging the telescope.

q: 26. For which of the following permanent adjustments of theodolite, the spire test is used?
options: Adjustment of altitude bubble and vertical index frame
explain: The spire test is used to check and adjust the horizontal (trunnion) axis of a theodolite, ensuring it is truly perpendicular to the vertical axis, by sighting a high point in both faces.

q: 27. A traverse survey can be plotted
options: by rectangular coordinates or plotting by tangents
by paper protractor or by included angles
by parallel meridian method or plotting by chords
explain: All the mentioned methods are valid ways to transfer field traverse data onto paper.

q: 28. The most commonly used set of theodolite operations are
explain: As per the book's answer key, the most commonly used operational combination is right face and right swing.

q: 29. The included angles of a theodolite traverse, are generally measured
explain: As per the book's answer key, included angles in a theodolite traverse are generally measured anti-clockwise from the forward station.

q: 30. If 'n' is the number of sides, then the total sum of interior angles of a closed traverse should be
explain: The sum of interior angles of a closed polygon of n sides is given by the standard geometric formula (2n - 4) x 90 degrees.

q: 31. The angular error of closure or summation error should not exceed
options: 3√N where N is number of stations or sides.
explain: The standard permissible angular closure error in compass surveying is typically defined as 15' multiplied by the square root of the number of stations.

q: 32. If 'n' is the number of sides, then the total sum of exterior angles of a closed traverse should be
explain: Since interior and exterior angles at each vertex are supplementary and their total for all n vertices is 4 right angles more than the interior sum, the sum of exterior angles works out to (2n + 4) x 90 degrees.

q: 33. In locating the details of inaccessible objects visible at least from transit stations, the method used is
options: by angles and distances from the same station
by angle from one station and distance from the other station
by distances from two different stations
explain: Note: this answer-key entry appears mismatched with the adjacent question in the book. The standard method for locating inaccessible objects visible from two transit stations is by angles from both stations (intersection); please verify this entry visually against your copy.

q: 34. In a transit theodolite error due to eccentricity of verniers is counteracted by
options: reading different parts of main scale
taking both right swing and left swing reading
explain: The error due to eccentricity of verniers (misalignment of the vernier scale centre with the instrument's rotation axis) is counteracted by reading both verniers (typically 180 degrees apart) and averaging the results.

q: 35. According to Bowditch Rule, the correction to latitude (or departure) of any side is equal to
options: Length of the side / Perimeter of traverse
Perimeter of traverse / Length of the side
Total error in latitude / Perimeter of traverse
Total error in latitude x Length of that side / Perimeter of traverse
explain: Bowditch's rule states that the correction to the latitude (or departure) of a side is proportional to the length of that side: Correction = Total error in latitude x (Length of that side / Perimeter of traverse).

q: 36. Right face and left reading are taken to
options: eliminate error of trunnion axis not exactly horizontal
eliminate error in the line of collimation
explain: Taking readings on both faces (face left and face right) of the theodolite and averaging eliminates multiple instrumental errors together - collimation error, trunnion axis error, and other index errors - so all of the above apply.

q: 37. Which of the following methods of theodolite traversing is suitable for locating the details which are far away from transit stations?
options: by measuring angle to the point from at least three stations
by measuring angles to the point from at least two stations
by measuring angel at one station and distance from other
by measuring distance from two points on traverse line
explain: Distant details, which cannot be directly chained, are located by the method of intersection, measuring angles to the point from at least two known theodolite stations.

q: 38. Axis of altitude level is
options: parallel to the line of collimation
explain: The axis of the altitude (vertical circle) level is set parallel to the line of collimation, so that when the bubble is centred, the line of sight reads a true zero (horizontal) on the vertical circle.

q: 39. A 15 cm theodolite means
options: length of the telescope is 15 cm
diameter of lower plate is 15 cm
radius of upper plate is 15 cm
explain: A theodolite is designated by the diameter of its lower (graduated horizontal) plate; a '15 cm theodolite' has a lower plate diameter of 15 cm.

q: 40. In precision theodolite traverse for roads and railways, the angular error of closure should not exceed
explain: For a precision theodolite traverse suitable for roads and railways, the permissible angular error of closure is 1 minute multiplied by the square root of the number of stations (N).

q: 41. The length of a traverse line (L) may be obtained by
options: L = Latitude x secant of reduced bearing
L = Departure x cosecant of reduced bearing
explain: The length of a traverse line can be computed from its latitude and departure using any of several equivalent trigonometric relations, hence any one of the above methods gives the correct length.

q: 42. A traverse deflection angle is
options: the difference between the included angle and 180
the difference between 360 and the included angle
explain: A deflection angle is defined as the angle by which a survey line deviates from the prolongation of the preceding line, calculated as the difference between the included angle and 180 degrees.

q: 43. An angle of deflection right, may be directly obtained by setting the instrument to read
explain: To directly obtain a deflection angle right, the theodolite is set to read 180 degrees when backsighted to the previous station, so that the forward reading directly gives the deflection angle.

q: 44. Left swing is not much favoured in theodolite survey because
options: most of the surveyors are accustomed to right hand
it is inconvenient to turn the telescope anti-clockwise
vertical scale comes to an inconvenient position to be read
explain: Left swing is generally avoided in practice because most surveyors are more accustomed and comfortable operating the instrument with their right hand for a clockwise (right) swing.

q: 45. You have to observe an included angle with better accuracy than what is achievable by vernier, you will prefer the method of
explain: The method of repetition allows an angle to be measured multiple times cumulatively on the graduated circle before reading, effectively increasing the precision beyond the least count of the vernier.

q: 46. Centering error of a theodolite produces an error
options: which does not vary with the direction or pointing
which varies with the direction of pointing and inversely with the length of sight
explain: A centering error causes an angular error that varies depending on the direction of pointing and is inversely proportional to the length of the sight - shorter sights are affected more severely.

q: 47. Which of the following errors can be eliminated by taking mean of both face observations?
options: Errors due to eccentricity of verniers
Errors due to imperfect adjustments of plate levels
Errors due to line of collimation not being perpendicular to horizontal axis
explain: Taking the mean of face left and face right observations eliminates errors due to the line of collimation not being perfectly perpendicular to the horizontal axis, since this error reverses sign between the two faces.

q: 48. For which of the following permanent adjustments of theodolite, the spire test is used?
explain: The spire test is specifically used to check and adjust the horizontal (trunnion) axis of a theodolite, ensuring it is truly horizontal by sighting a high point from both faces.

q: 49. Which of the following error is not eliminated by the method of repetition of horizontal angle measurement?
options: Error due to eccentricity of verniers
Error due to displacement of station signals
Error due to wrong adjustment of line of collimation and trunnion axis
explain: The method of repetition eliminates errors due to inaccurate graduation and instrumental maladjustments by accumulating readings around the circle, but it does not eliminate the error due to eccentricity of verniers.

q: 50. The angle between the prolongation of the preceding line and the forward line of a traverse is called
explain: As defined earlier (Q210), this angle between the prolongation of the preceding survey line and the following line is the deflection angle.
